pillar_reactions.evidence: Tied it to his own constraints unprompted and pre-sold himself on the format before the rep finished: 'I like what he described, you know, you could do it on 45 minutes to an hour. Now that's very appealing to me. I'd rather more intensity and less time because I don't have that much time.' Also extended the rep's portability point himself — 'Plus you can do it anywhere, right? You don't have to go to a gym, you can bring a kettlebell with you' — and closed the phase-two pitch with 'That's what I'm looking for. Exactly.'

The weakest fit of the three and he tested it immediately. Volunteered 'I've been a for 20 years, though. So I mean, I have that part figured out' (vegetarian), then asked the direct compatibility question: 'Does he customize it for vegetarians?' The rep said yes and that any dietary restriction is fully customised. Unresolved tension the rep did not address: the pillar is pitched as 'eating like our ancestors would' and the prospect has been meat-free for two decades.

This is what he came for and he said so three separate times before any pitch: 'I need somebody to hold me accountable, because that's my main moral weakness, I suppose'; 'everybody needs a little accountability once in a while, and so I realize an external force might be the thing to get me off my a little bit'; and the sports metaphor he built himself — 'I'm a good enough coach to get me this far, but I'm not a championship coach.'

anchors.raw: that's around what I expected it to be. So it's not earth shattering.
anchors.note: He had pre-set his own expectation upward before the number landed — 'I'm sure it's not cheap, so, you know, hit me with the cost.' The $9,000 met an anchor he had already built himself from two years of following Trevor, which is why there was no price objection, only a budget-timing one.

anchors.raw: I have a home gym. I've spent a long time and a lot of money outfitting it. So I have pretty much everything I need. I just don't have the knowledge, necessarily, to utilize it.
anchors.note: Established habit of spending materially on his own fitness, and the spend is stranded without instruction — the strongest value argument available on this call. The rep never used it.

anchors.raw: I've bought a program here and there and I, you know, but it's all, you here's the program, go for it. You know, I've never had a coach like that.
anchors.note: Self-serve programmes are the cheap substitute in his head and he has already ruled them out as insufficient. This removes the usual price-comparison risk, but the rep never asked what those cost or what happened with them, so it was never converted into value.

anchors.raw: if I spent 9,000 bucks and then talk to my wife, I think, I think she'd be angry and I don't need that kind of aggravation
anchors.note: The real barrier is not the money but a household rule about unilateral spend at this size. Mitigating fact the rep noticed but did not exploit: the wife already follows Trevor on Instagram and already knew the call was happening.

unmet_demand.want: Conditioning specific to long-distance hiking with a loaded pack, building toward multi-day trail work in his late 60s
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep asserted 'your cardio endurance 100%' but nothing in the three phases addresses load carriage or sustained low-intensity duration; the offer is 30-40 minute kettlebell sessions. Whether the programme actually produces trail endurance for a 61-year-old is unestablished either way.

unmet_demand.want: A vegetarian version of the Primal Eating Protocol, which is explicitly framed around ancestral eating
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep said it is fully customised for vegetarians and vegans, so this is probably served — but the pillar's own positioning ('eating like our ancestors would', 'what foods to eat, to build your muscle, even as a vegetarian') actively works against a 20-year vegetarian and nobody reconciled the two.

unmet_demand.want: A concrete monthly instalment figure he could take to his wife
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Payment plans and financing were mentioned in the abstract — six-month internal splits, interest added on 12-month plans, third-party month-to-month — but no rate, instalment amount or total was ever quoted, so the decision he took to his wife was framed as a single $9,000 outlay.
